levels.title: Level 1: The Magic Vowels (A, E, I, O, U)

slides.title: What are Vowels?
slides.subtitle: The special 5 letters that bring words to life!
slides.keyConcept: The 5 English vowels are A, E, I, O, and U. Every single English word has at least one vowel sound!
points: Vowels make open-mouth sounds without teeth or lips blocking airflow.
Each vowel can make a SHORT sound (Cat, Bed, Pig) or a LONG sound (Cake, Tree, Bike).
Long vowels say their own name! (A says /eɪ/, E says /iː/, I says /aɪ/, O says /oʊ/, U says /juː/).

example.problem: Which of these letters is a vowel: B, M, E, or T?
example.note: A, E, I, O, U are vowels. All other letters are consonants.

slides.title: Short Vowels vs. Long Vowels
slides.subtitle: Listen closely to the magic difference!
slides.keyConcept: A short vowel sound is quick and bouncy. A long vowel sound says the letter's name!
points: A: Short /æ/ in Apple & Hat vs. Long /eɪ/ in Cake & Rain.
E: Short /ɛ/ in Egg & Bed vs. Long /iː/ in Eagle & Feet.
I: Short /ɪ/ in Igloo & Fish vs. Long /aɪ/ in Ice & Kite.
O: Short /ɒ/ in Octopus & Pot vs. Long /oʊ/ in Ocean & Boat.
U: Short /ʌ/ in Umbrella & Cup vs. Long /juː/ in Uniform & Cube.

example.problem: Does CAT have a short or long 'A' sound?
example.note: C-A-T makes the bouncy /æ/ sound, not the /eɪ/ sound in Cake.

levels.title: Level 2: Early Consonants (B, C, D, F, G)

slides.title: Consonant Sounds B, C, D, F, G
slides.subtitle: Building the foundation of reading!
slides.keyConcept: Consonants are voiced or unvoiced sounds made by blocking airflow with tongue, teeth, or lips.
points: B makes the bouncing /b/ sound (Ball, Bat, Bear).
C makes the hard /k/ sound (Cat, Cup) or soft /s/ sound (City).
D makes the tapping /d/ sound (Dog, Duck, Drum).
F makes the blowing /f/ sound (Fish, Frog, Fan).
G makes the hard /ɡ/ sound (Goat, Girl) or soft /dʒ/ sound (Gem).

levels.title: Level 3: Middle Consonants (H, J, K, L, M, N)

slides.title: Consonant Sounds H, J, K, L, M, N
slides.subtitle: Expanding your sound universe!
slides.keyConcept: Learn how to form H, J, K, L, M, and N with your voice and mouth!
points: H makes the whispering /h/ sound like breathing out (Hat, House).
J makes the bouncy /dʒ/ sound (Jam, Jelly, Jump).
K makes the crisp /k/ sound (Kite, King, Kangaroo).
L makes the tongue-tapping /l/ sound (Lion, Lemon, Leaf).
M makes the lips-closed humming /m/ sound (Moon, Milk, Monkey).
N makes the tongue-roof humming /n/ sound (Nest, Net, Nut).

points: P makes the puffing /p/ sound (Pen, Pig, Pizza).
Q is almost always paired with U to make the /kw/ sound (Queen, Quick, Quilt).
R makes the roaring /r/ sound (Rabbit, Ring, Rainbow).
S makes the hissing /s/ sound (Sun, Snake, Star).
T makes the tapping /t/ sound (Tiger, Tree, Tent).

slides.title: Consonant Sounds V, W, X, Y, Z & Digraphs
slides.subtitle: Complete your master reading journey!
slides.keyConcept: Finish all 26 alphabet sounds and discover how two letters team up to make brand new sounds (Digraphs)!
points: V vibrates your lower lip: /v/ (Van, Violin, Vase).
W rounds your lips: /w/ (Water, Watch, Wind).
X makes the /ks/ sound, usually found at the end of words (Fox, Box, Six).
Y makes the /j/ sound (Yellow, Yo-yo, Yarn).
Z makes the buzzing /z/ sound (Zebra, Zoo, Zipper).
Digraphs: SH /ʃ/ (Ship), CH /tʃ/ (Chair), TH /θ/ (Thumb).

example.note: S and H combine to make the quiet /ʃ/ sound.
